list.intro: Madagascar is a continent in miniature. Explore each region, find the places worth the drive and pick the right month.

ambanja.name: Ambanja
ambanja.tagline: Cocoa valleys and the gateway to Nosy Be
intro: Ambanja sits in the green Sambirano valley, one of the island’s best-known cocoa-growing areas. Plantations, spice fields and river villages surround the town.
Most travellers pass through on the way to Nosy Be, but a day or two here shows you the working countryside behind the beaches.
ambanja.getting: By road from Diego Suarez or by domestic flight and road via Nosy Be. Boats to Nosy Be leave from the nearby Ankify jetty.

todo.title: Visit a cocoa plantation
todo.text: Follow the beans from tree to drying rack and taste fresh chocolate.

todo.title: Walk through spice fields
todo.text: Meet growers of vanilla, pepper and ylang-ylang with a local guide.

todo.title: Browse the town market
todo.text: Fruit, spices and crafts, best early in the morning.

visit.name: Sambirano valley
visit.text: Rolling plantations and river views, ideal by car or bike.
details: The Sambirano valley is the green heart of the region, with cocoa, coffee and spice farms along the river.
Drive or cycle the back roads, stop in villages and ask growers to show you how each crop is harvested.
overview: The Sambirano valley is the green heart of the Ambanja region. Cocoa, coffee, vanilla and ylang-ylang grow side by side along the river, and the valley has long been known for its fine cocoa.
Your day follows quiet back roads between plantations and villages. You stop where something is happening: beans drying in the sun, a family harvesting pods, a stall selling fruit.
A local guide travels with you, translates, and introduces you to the growers, so you leave with real conversations and not only photos.
highlights: Follow cocoa from tree to drying rack
Taste fresh chocolate and local vanilla
Cycle or drive through river villages
Stop at roadside fruit and spice stalls

visit.name: Manongarivo reserve
visit.text: A protected forest for hikers who want wildlife and quiet.
details: Manongarivo is a protected forest reserve in the mountains behind Ambanja, rich in plants and wildlife.
Access takes planning, so we arrange guides and permits before your visit.
overview: Manongarivo is a protected forest reserve in the mountains behind Ambanja, home to a wide range of plants, birds and lemurs.
Trails are rough and access takes planning, so this visit suits walkers who enjoy quiet and are comfortable with basic conditions.
We arrange the guide, permits and transport in advance, and adapt the route to the season and the group.
highlights: Walk forest trails with a trained guide
Look for lemurs, chameleons and birds
Spot endemic plants along the path
Small groups for a quiet experience

visit.name: Ankify jetty
visit.text: The departure point for boats to Nosy Be.
details: Ankify is the small port where boats leave for Nosy Be, about an hour’s drive from Ambanja.
The crossing takes around an hour by speedboat, and schedules depend on tides and weather.
does: Take the boat to Nosy Be
overview: Ankify is the small port where boats leave for Nosy Be. It sits about an hour by road from Ambanja, on a calm stretch of coast.
The crossing takes around an hour by speedboat. Times depend on tides and weather, so we confirm schedules the day before.
Arrive early to enjoy a meal by the water, then cross to Nosy Be with your luggage handled by our team.
highlights: Scenic drive from Ambanja to the coast
Lunch by the water before departure

ambanja.tip: Ask us to arrange a plantation visit in advance, as harvest and drying seasons change what you can see.

ramena-beach.name: Ramena Beach
ramena-beach.tagline: Sailing, kitesurfing and the Emerald Sea
intro: Ramena is a small fishing village on the bay of Diego Suarez, known for calm turquoise water and steady winds.
It is an easy day trip from town, or a relaxed base for a few days of sailing and watersports.
ramena-beach.getting: About 30 minutes by road from Diego Suarez. Taxis and private drivers make the trip daily.

todo.title: Sail across the bay
todo.text: Half-day and full-day boat trips with swimming stops.

todo.title: Try kitesurfing
todo.text: Lessons and rentals for all levels on the nearby beaches.

todo.title: Eat fresh seafood
todo.text: Simple beach restaurants serve the morning catch.

visit.name: Emerald Sea
visit.text: Shallow, bright water, best reached by boat.

visit.name: Sugar Loaf
visit.text: The iconic rock rising from Diego Bay.

visit.name: Dunes Bay
visit.text: Wind and white sand for kitesurfers.

ramena-beach.tip: Winds are strongest in the afternoon, so plan boat trips for the morning.

nosy-iranja.name: Nosy Iranja
intro: Nosy Iranja is a pair of small islands joined by a long sandbar that appears at low tide. Sea turtles nest on its beaches.
It is reached by boat from Nosy Be, usually as a full-day trip or an overnight stay.
nosy-iranja.getting: By speedboat or sailboat from Nosy Be, roughly two hours depending on the sea.

todo.title: Walk the sandbar
todo.text: Cross between the two islands at low tide.

todo.title: Snorkel with turtles
todo.text: Calm, clear water close to the beach.

todo.title: Climb to the lighthouse
todo.text: A short walk for views over the whole area.

visit.name: The sandbar
visit.text: The signature view of the island.

visit.name: Turtle beach
visit.text: A protected nesting area, visit with respect.

visit.name: Nosy Lonjo
visit.text: A quiet neighbouring island, often combined in one trip.

nosy-iranja.tip: Check tide times before you go, since the sandbar is only visible at low tide.

antananarivo.name: Antananarivo
antananarivo.tagline: A hillside capital full of markets and history
intro: Antananarivo climbs a series of hills, with narrow streets, old palaces and busy markets.
Most journeys start here, so plan a day or two to acclimatise and explore.
antananarivo.getting: International flights arrive at Ivato airport, about 30 minutes from the centre.

todo.title: Explore the old town
todo.text: Walk the steep lanes of the upper city.

todo.title: Visit the Rova
todo.text: The former royal palace above the city.

visit.name: The Rova
visit.text: A hilltop royal compound with wide views.

visit.name: Lake Anosy
visit.text: A calm spot in the city centre.

visit.name: Ambohimanga
visit.text: A sacred royal hill a short drive north.

antananarivo.tip: Traffic is heavy, so allow extra time for airport transfers.

baobab-avenue.name: Baobab Avenue
intro: Near Morondava, a dirt road runs between tall baobab trees, some hundreds of years old.
It is one of the most photographed places in Madagascar, and it is best at sunrise and sunset.
baobab-avenue.getting: By road or domestic flight to Morondava, then a short drive of about 45 minutes.

todo.title: Watch the sunset
todo.text: The light turns the trunks orange and red.

todo.title: Meet local villagers
todo.text: Visit nearby hamlets with a guide.

visit.name: The main avenue
visit.text: The famous line of tall trees.

visit.name: Twin baobabs
visit.text: Two trunks twisted around each other.

baobab-avenue.tip: Arrive an hour before sunset to walk the avenue before the crowds.

andasibe.name: Andasibe
intro: Andasibe is a rainforest reserve known for the indri, the largest living lemur, whose calls carry across the forest.
It is close enough to the capital for a weekend, and better with a night walk.
andasibe.getting: About three to four hours by road from Antananarivo.

todo.title: Track the indri
todo.text: A guided morning walk to find a family group.

todo.title: Take a night walk
todo.text: Spot small nocturnal lemurs and chameleons.

todo.title: Visit a lemur island
todo.text: Meet rescued lemurs in a sheltered setting.

visit.name: Andasibe-Mantadia
visit.text: The main national park and its forest trails.

visit.name: Lemur island
visit.text: A short boat ride to close encounters.

andasibe.tip: Bring a light rain jacket, since the forest is humid all year.
